definitions.explanation: A strap or handle that hangs from above for standing passengers to hold on a train or bus; also a hanging handle on a bag or fixture.

examples.english: to hold on to the hanging strap.

examples.japanese: {電車|でんしゃ}が{揺|ゆ}れたので、とっさにつり{手|て}を{握|にぎ}った。
examples.english: The train shook, so I instinctively gripped the strap.

examples.japanese: {満員|まんいん}{電車|でんしゃ}で、つり{手|て}にも{手|て}が{届|とど}かないほど{混|こ}んでいた。
examples.english: The train was so packed that I couldn't even reach a hanging strap.

notes:
Written {吊|つ}り{手|て} or つり{手|て}, from {吊|つ}る (to hang, to suspend) + {手|て} (handle). Most often refers to the loop straps hanging in trains and buses for standing passengers.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- つり{手|て}につかまる: to hold on to the strap
- つり{手|て}を{握|にぎ}る: to grip the strap

SIMILAR WORDS:
- つり{革|かわ}: strap hanger — the same train strap, naming the (originally leather) loop
- {手|て}すり: handrail — a fixed rail, not a hanging strap
